title: A finite purely inseparable extension is a tower of p-th roots
statement: Let $p$ be a prime number, $F$ a field of characteristic $p$ and $E/F$ a finite purely inseparable field extension [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension] [def-pc-field-extension]. Then there are elements $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_n\in E$ ($n\ge0$) with $E=F(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_n)$ such that for $i=1,\dots,n$, writing $F_{i-1}=F(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_{i-1})$ ($F_0=F$): $\alpha_i^p\in F_{i-1}$, $\alpha_i^p$ is not a $p$-th power in $F_{i-1}$, and $[F_{i-1}(\alpha_i):F_{i-1}]=p$. In particular, if $E\ne F$, then $M=F_{n-1}$ is an intermediate field $F\subseteq M\subsetneq E$, finite and purely inseparable over $F$ with $[M:F]<[E:F]$, and $E=M(\beta)$ with $\beta=\alpha_n$, $\beta^p\in M$ not a $p$-th power in $M$, and $E\cong M[z]/(z^p-\beta^p)$ as $M$-algebras.

source.place: Fields, Lemma Tag 09HI (lemma-finite-purely-inseparable, line 1669) and its proof (Lemmas nr-roots-unchanged, take-pth-root); used without citation in the proof of More on Algebra Proposition 07PM ('Let K subset M subset L be a subfield such that L is a degree p extension of M obtained by adjoining a pth root of an element f in M')
